Two things that arrow hides. OnAdd also fires for every Pod in the informer's INITIAL LIST (IsInInitialList), so on
an operator restart a large application replays all its existing executors as Creates - the debounce below absorbs
that into one reconcile. And the event carries no count: it is purely a trigger to go and look.

This is the whole inference. There is no DA event and no call from Spark into Kueue: the desired executor count is
re-derived from live Pod objects on every debounced reconcile, and cached for the pass (podset.go:194). The derived
count is then clamped to Dynamic Allocation's own minExecutors/maxExecutors (podset.go:356).
